name: Grand River Aseptic Manufacturing
old_description: Inside GRAM’s New Groninger Syringe & Cartridge Filling Line: What Modern Fill-Finish Technology Means for Biologic Drug Manufacturers
about:
The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but it presents itself as a contract development and manufacturing organization focused on sterile injectable fill-finish.

GRAM runs five filling lines equipped with isolator technology, handling liquid and lyophilized vials, prefilled syringes, and cartridges. The site supports formulation volumes up to 1,000 liters and offers low- and high-speed filling, lyophilization with auto-loader, single-use and product-dedicated equipment, terminal sterilization, automated through manual inspection, labeling, packaging, serialization, aggregation, analytical testing, and regulatory support. Three of its five facilities are designed to meet revised EU GMP Annex 1 requirements.

The CDMO serves pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies developing biologics, small molecules, and vaccines, from clinical trials through commercial supply. It also partners with drug-delivery device innovators to tailor fill-finish for autoinjectors and on-body delivery systems.

GRAM emphasizes its team’s collaborative relationships and agility as differentiators, stating that clients consider its approach unique in the pharma industry. The company’s mission centers on delivering high-quality injectable solutions with reliability to advance patient care.

name: Graphic Packaging International
old_description: Our next generation packaging solutions create memorable moments now
about:
Graphic Packaging International is headquartered in West Monroe, Louisiana. The company operates as part of Graphic Packaging Holding Company, a publicly traded corporation. Public materials do not disclose a founding year or founder names.

The company manufactures consumer packaging solutions with a focus on paperboard. Its product portfolio includes proprietary systems such as CleanClose™ child-resistant detergent packaging, Boardio™ rigid paperboard canisters, KeelClip™ clip-style multipack cartons that replace plastic rings, PaperSeal™ barrier-lined trays for modified-atmosphere applications, and ProducePack™ recyclable punnet trays for fresh produce. Graphic Packaging runs a global network of more than 100 paperboard manufacturing facilities, packaging plants, design and innovation centers, and regional offices, employing over 23,000 people and holding roughly 3,000 patents.

Customers span foodservice, pet care, e-commerce, beverage, household detergents, and fresh produce. The company cites collaborations with brands such as BETTERGUARDS for sports-technology packaging and Smithy Mushrooms for exotic mushroom punnets. Its packaging also serves detergent pods, beverage multipacks, and modified-atmosphere food trays.

Graphic Packaging positions itself as a leader in sustainable consumer packaging, emphasizing renewable, recycled, and recyclable materials. It promotes a Design for the Environment approach and highlights innovations that replace plastic with paperboard alternatives, aiming to reduce environmental impact while maintaining performance.

name: Great Plains Renewables
old_description: Before starting repairs, we consult with the manufacturer of your equipment to ensure that every repair is properly executed.
about:
Great Plains Renewables operates from Yutan, Nebraska, providing solar energy solutions across an eight-state region that includes Nebraska, Iowa, Kansas, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, North Dakota, and South Dakota. The company has been a member of the industry directory since 2022, though its founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The firm delivers end-to-end solar services encompassing development, engineering, installation, and ongoing management for residential, commercial, and agricultural clients. Its offerings include solar panel repair and maintenance, battery backup system installation, portable solar power equipment such as Jackery products, and cold storage system integration. The company also handles storm damage repairs and assists customers with financing options.

Great Plains Renewables serves three primary customer segments: farms seeking to reduce operating costs through solar, businesses aiming for energy independence, and homeowners looking to lower their carbon footprint. Concrete examples from its project portfolio include agricultural installations that boost yields, commercial rooftop arrays, and residential battery backup systems for grid resilience.

The company distinguishes itself by consulting directly with equipment manufacturers before performing any repair, ensuring that each fix aligns with original specifications. Its stated mission is to help clients power their properties with a renewable energy mix tailored to their specific needs, leveraging experience across development, engineering, installation, and management to deliver community-focused solutions.

name: Great Planes Millwork
old_description: Elevating Spaces with Reproduction Molding & Fine Woodworking
about:
After years of study and participation in woodworking clubs in Des Moines and Ames, Ulrich established a workshop focused on handcrafted solid-wood pieces.

The shop specializes in reproduction moulding that matches historic architectural profiles, custom furniture and cabinets, end-grain cutting boards, and a range of one-off wooden items such as display easels, picture frames, and golf-ball display cases. Each piece starts with hand-selected hardwoods and moves through a milling process overseen directly by Ulrich.

The customer base is primarily residential, including homeowners seeking to restore period details or commission heirloom-quality furniture. Testimonials reference projects like matching existing crown moulding in a home and building a custom golf-ball display cabinet for a family.

Ulrich emphasizes that the business avoids mass production; every item is made by hand with a collaborative design phase that puts the client at the center. The company stands behind its work with a satisfaction guarantee, citing passion and attention to detail as its defining traits.

name: Great Sky Solar
old_description: with honest guidance, skilled craftsmanship, and genuine care for every home.
about:
Great Sky Solar was founded in 2026 and is headquartered in Lexington, Massachusetts. The company operates as a locally focused installer serving the Greater Boston area with solar photovoltaic and heat pump systems.

The firm designs and installs custom solar arrays and electric heat pumps using in-house crews rather than subcontractors. Its process includes a custom design phase, a good-faith agreement with zero deposit, a dedicated project manager, expert installation, and ongoing lifetime system support. To date the team of 10-plus local experts has completed more than 2,980 installations representing over 30 megawatts of installed capacity.

Great Sky Solar works primarily with residential homeowners and commercial property owners in Massachusetts who want to generate their own clean energy. The company references hundreds of neighbors who have switched to solar and highlights installations on both homes and businesses.

The company positions itself as a departure from volume-driven sales models, emphasizing transparent guidance, no-commission advisors, and a 30-year insurance-backed warranty that covers failures, labor costs, and even insolvency risk. Its stated mission is to align clean energy with clean business practices, prioritizing long-term accountability over short-term growth.

name: Green Hills Metal Werks
old_description: Metal art sculptures made locally to dress up your yard and make your neighbors jealous.
about:
Green Hills Metal Werks operates from Dousman, Wisconsin. The business took shape when owner Jake, who had been welding since purchasing his first welder at 14, acquired a CNC plasma table and began turning his fabrication experience into a commercial venture.

The shop produces commercial and residential signage, garden art sculptures, custom metal fabrications, and short-run production parts. Core processes include CNC plasma cutting, welding, and hand-finishing, with capabilities spanning structural and ornamental metalwork, handrails, backlit signs, water features, and decorative wall art. The company serves customers across Southeast Wisconsin, including Oconomowoc, Waukesha, Milwaukee, and Madison.

Clients range from businesses needing monument, projecting, or wall-mounted signs to homeowners commissioning personal/family signs, ranch and farm markers, garden fountains, and memorial pieces. The portfolio also includes interior and exterior decor for cabins and lodges.

Jake emphasizes a design-to-finish approach, offering custom designs crafted by hand and maintaining licensed, bonded, and insured status. The operation was built on the idea of helping customers bring their ideas to reality through artistic metalwork.

name: Green Mountain Electric Supply
old_description: For the best experience on our site, be sure to turn on Javascript in your browser.
about:
Green Mountain Electric Supply traces its roots to 1953, when Earl Laber, Raymond Place, and Norman Bean opened a motor repair and rewinding shop in Newport, Vermont. By the mid-1960s the partners had expanded into selling electrical supplies to factories across northeastern Vermont. In 1970 the business was renamed Green Mountain Electric Supply, Inc., and after Place and Bean retired, Laber ran the company until 1977, when he sold it to his three sons—Gary, Scott, and Gregg—and partner Steven Carpenter, establishing a second-generation, family-owned operation.

The company shifted entirely to wholesale distribution in 1986, abandoning motor repair to focus on electrical supplies. A 12,000-square-foot warehouse was built in Newport in 1988 and later expanded to 23,000 square feet with a showroom and offices. Through a series of acquisitions—Choiniere Electric (2001), Burgess Electrical Supply (2004), Glens Falls Electric Supply (2008), Valley Electric Supply (2010), and Red Hook Electric Supply (2016)—GMES grew to operate branches across Vermont, New Hampshire, and New York, with corporate offices established in Colchester, Vermont, in 2014. A renewable energies division launched in 2011 added photovoltaic solar sales to the product lineup.

Today GMES serves contractors, builders, industrial facilities, and DIY enthusiasts throughout the Northeast, offering a broad range of lighting, heating and cooling equipment, electrical conduit, and solar components. The company emphasizes competitive pricing, a deep inventory spread across multiple locations, and a knowledgeable sales team to assist with product selection.

The firm’s stated differentiation rests on its extensive local presence, delivery capabilities, and a commitment to customer service that includes online account management, educational resources, and specialized solar expertise.

name: Green Wave Solar
old_description: Harness the sun's power with Green Wave Solar's expert solar energy solutions. Eliminate high energy bills and step into a sustainable future.
about:
Green Wave Solar is based in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, and serves homeowners and businesses across the Middle Tennessee region, including Nashville, Rutherford County, Chattanooga, and McMinnville. The company operates under the LJC Holdings LLC entity and has built a reputation for responsive solar energy services throughout the Tennessee Valley.

The firm provides turnkey solar solutions for both residential and commercial clients. Its service portfolio spans solar panel installation, battery backup systems, panel repair and replacement, equipment sales, EV charging station integration, and consulting on incentives and rebates. The company also offers utility-scale solar services for larger projects.

Customers range from individual homeowners seeking energy independence to commercial property owners aiming to reduce operational costs and meet sustainability goals. The company's project references include installations for residents in Murfreesboro, Smyrna, and Brentwood, as well as commercial clients across Rutherford County and the broader Nashville metro area.

Green Wave Solar distinguishes itself through NABCEP certification, which signals adherence to industry-recognized installation standards. The company also promotes a veteran's discount, a $500 referral program, and a $1,000 local discount, emphasizing community-focused pricing alongside its five-star review standing on Google, Facebook, and EnergySage.
